newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says won't resort to oil price controls.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says won't resort to oil price controls.

text.p: Thailand will not resort to control of domestic oil prices to curb inflation following the baht's flotation last week, an official at state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) said on Wednesday.
The de facto devaluation which saw the baht depreciating by 15-20 percent since it was cut loose from a fixed exchange regime on July 2 is expected to drive oil prices higher.

Thailand will let state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand and Bangchak Petroleum Plc set higher benchmarks for the market with their prices, the official said. Details were not immediately available.

The decision was made during a meeting between the government and oil companies on Tuesday. At that meeting, the government secured a promise from the industry that it would raise local retail prices according to changes in exchange rates following the new baht regime, the official said.
Thailand has floated its domestic oil prices since 1991.
Retail oil prices in many stations, including those of PTT and Bangchak, are expected to rise by 15-20 satang per litre by the end of this week, the official said.
Industry sources estimate that the extra cost to oil companies at an exchange rate of 28 baht per dollar was about 25 satang per litre.
